register: Formal political and social-theory adjective, often critical, for an actor or worldview that establishes durable leadership and dominance.
trap: Hegemónico is more specific than merely dominante: in critical theory it can include making a particular worldview appear natural or consensual.
example_tl: El relato hegemónico presenta la extracción masiva de datos como precio inevitable de la innovación y excluye del debate cualquier alternativa regulatoria.
example_en: The hegemonic narrative presents mass data extraction as the inevitable price of innovation and excludes any regulatory alternative from the debate.
cloze: El relato {{c1::hegemónico}} presenta la extracción masiva de datos como precio inevitable de la innovación y excluye del debate cualquier alternativa regulatoria.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Retention is justified by the term's specific critical-theory sense rather than by cognate recognition alone.

register: Formal-critical adjective for harm that advances gradually or unobtrusively and is therefore difficult to recognise or resist.
trap: Insidioso does not mean merely peligroso or engañoso; it highlights concealed, gradual harm whose consequences may become visible only later.
example_tl: El efecto insidioso de la personalización consiste en reducir paulatinamente la diversidad informativa sin que el usuario perciba una restricción explícita.
example_en: The insidious effect of personalisation consists in gradually reducing information diversity without the user perceiving an explicit restriction.
cloze: El efecto {{c1::insidioso}} de la personalización consiste en reducir paulatinamente la diversidad informativa sin que el usuario perciba una restricción explícita.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate; the note retains the marked adjective to establish the covert, cumulative component of its meaning.

register: Neutral-formal in literary, cultural and political criticism for a setting or development resembling an oppressive imagined society.
trap: Spanish adapts the English y to i and marks the stress: distópico, not *dystópico or *distopico.
example_tl: El escenario distópico no surge de una máquina omnipotente, sino de miles de decisiones administrativas que convierten la vigilancia en rutina.
example_en: The dystopian scenario does not arise from an omnipotent machine, but from thousands of administrative decisions that turn surveillance into routine.
cloze: El escenario {{c1::distópico}} no surge de una máquina omnipotente, sino de miles de decisiones administrativas que convierten la vigilancia en rutina.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from its failure to expose the Spanish spelling and stress pattern.

register: Neutral technical and policy adjective for a process or system performed through automation rather than direct case-by-case human action.
trap: Automatizado and automático overlap but are not mechanically interchangeable: automatizado emphasises a process converted to automation, as in decisión automatizada.
example_tl: El sistema automatizado rechazó miles de solicitudes porque el modelo heredaba criterios históricos que penalizaban a los barrios con menor renta.
example_en: The automated system rejected thousands of applications because the model inherited historical criteria that penalised lower-income neighbourhoods.
cloze: El sistema {{c1::automatizado}} rechazó miles de solicitudes porque el modelo heredaba criterios históricos que penalizaban a los barrios con menor renta.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. Self-review rejected automático as an alternative because it would blur a useful distinction in automated-decision policy.

register: Neutral-formal in social and policy analysis for a phenomenon distributed broadly across places, systems or everyday practices.
trap: Do not default to penetrante: in abstract policy contexts it can sound physical, whereas generalizado or omnipresente conveys pervasive reach idiomatically.
example_tl: La vigilancia generalizada altera la conducta pública incluso cuando nadie sabe qué datos se recogen, durante cuánto tiempo ni con qué finalidad.
example_en: Pervasive surveillance alters public behaviour even when nobody knows what data is collected, for how long or for what purpose.
cloze: La vigilancia {{c1::generalizada}} altera la conducta pública incluso cuando nadie sabe qué datos se recogen, durante cuánto tiempo ni con qué finalidad.
note: The legacy omnipresente is valid and retained as an alternative; generalizado is the more idiomatic main choice for the policy collocation used here.

register: Learned neutral-formal adjective for something short-lived; fugaz is slightly less elevated and especially natural for attention or success.
trap: Italian effimero may prompt a doubled consonant; Spanish efímero has one f and carries a written accent on í.
example_tl: La atención efímera que generan las campañas virales rara vez sostiene reformas institucionales cuando desaparecen las imágenes que movilizaron al público.
example_en: The ephemeral attention generated by viral campaigns rarely sustains institutional reforms once the images that mobilised the public disappear.
cloze: La atención {{c1::efímera}} que generan las campañas virales rara vez sostiene reformas institucionales cuando desaparecen las imágenes que movilizaron al público.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. The example supplies feminine agreement, while the production headword remains the masculine lemma.

register: Formal-analytical construction for an outcome dependent on a stated condition; supeditado a is somewhat more emphatic about subordination.
trap: English contingent on is not normally *contingente en or *contingente sobre; use condicionado a, supeditado a or dependiente de.
example_tl: El acceso al mercado quedó condicionado al cumplimiento de auditorías independientes, no a las promesas voluntarias que la empresa formulaba cada trimestre.
example_en: Market access became contingent on compliance with independent audits, not on the voluntary promises the company made every quarter.
cloze: El acceso al mercado quedó {{c1::condicionado al}} cumplimiento de auditorías independientes, no a las promesas voluntarias que la empresa formulaba cada trimestre.
note: The isolated English prompt is polysemous. This note deliberately selects the high-value contingent-on sense; old_back contingente instead suggests possibility or non-necessity in Spanish.

register: Neutral-critical adjective for a person, message or design that influences others covertly or unfairly for its own ends.
trap: For an agentive design or tactic, manipulador is more idiomatic than simply mirroring English morphology as manipulativo, which is more restricted and technical.
example_tl: El diseño manipulador oculta la opción de rechazar el seguimiento y presenta la aceptación total como si fuera una decisión libre.
example_en: The manipulative design hides the option to reject tracking and presents full acceptance as if it were a free decision.
cloze: El diseño {{c1::manipulador}} oculta la opción de rechazar el seguimiento y presenta la aceptación total como si fuera una decisión libre.
note: Materially refines old_back manipulativo. Self-review selected the ordinary agentive adjective manipulador for the critical design context.

register: Formal-critical in political economy and technology criticism for a model that removes resources, data or value without comparable return.
trap: Extractivo is not automatically equivalent to explotador: the former describes a logic of extraction, while the latter explicitly foregrounds abuse.
example_tl: El modelo extractivo convierte la actividad cotidiana en datos privados y devuelve a las comunidades muy poco del valor económico generado.
example_en: The extractive model turns everyday activity into private data and returns very little of the economic value generated to communities.
cloze: El modelo {{c1::extractivo}} convierte la actividad cotidiana en datos privados y devuelve a las comunidades muy poco del valor económico generado.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. Retention is justified by the productive political-economy metaphor beyond literal resource industries.

register: Strongly critical but standard in analysis when used figuratively for a policy that ignores foreseeable or long-term consequences.
trap: Portuguese míope may prompt a false accent; Spanish miope has no written accent. Cortoplacista fits only when the criticism concerns time horizons.
example_tl: Una política miope subsidia centros de datos sin calcular su consumo hídrico ni la dependencia energética que consolidará durante décadas.
example_en: A myopic policy subsidises data centres without calculating their water consumption or the energy dependence it will entrench for decades.
cloze: Una política {{c1::miope}} subsidia centros de datos sin calcular su consumo hídrico ni la dependencia energética que consolidará durante décadas.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct. The example fixes the figurative policy sense rather than literal short-sightedness.

register: Formal philosophy and intellectual-history adjective referring to Hegel's thought, method or intellectual legacy.
trap: Spanish relational adjectives derived from personal names are normally lowercase: hegeliano, not *Hegeliano; the form also has only one g.
example_tl: El argumento hegeliano interpreta el conflicto como motor del cambio histórico, pero reduce las demandas de actores muy diversos a una síntesis única.
example_en: The Hegelian argument interprets conflict as the engine of historical change, but reduces the demands of very diverse actors to a single synthesis.
cloze: El argumento {{c1::hegeliano}} interpreta el conflicto como motor del cambio histórico, pero reduce las demandas de actores muy diversos a una síntesis única.
note: Corrects the unnecessary capitalisation in old_back; Spanish writes the relational adjective in lowercase. Self-review replaced simplifica actores with a more idiomatic construction.

register: Learned literary and analytical adjective, derived from Proteus, for something that repeatedly changes form, character or position.
trap: Proteico can also be read as relating to proteins; context must establish the Proteus-derived sense of changeability intended by English protean.
example_tl: El discurso proteico del movimiento adopta un lenguaje ecologista, nacionalista o tecnocrático según la audiencia, sin modificar su estructura de poder.
example_en: The movement's protean discourse adopts environmentalist, nationalist or technocratic language depending on the audience, without changing its power structure.
cloze: El discurso {{c1::proteico}} del movimiento adopta un lenguaje ecologista, nacionalista o tecnocrático según la audiencia, sin modificar su estructura de poder.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate but highly marked and polysemous; the note explicitly anchors the intended Proteus-derived sense. Self-review added the article required by the example's enumerated modifiers.

register: Formal analytical adjective for a pattern or result that departs from expectations and may therefore require explanation or investigation.
trap: Spanish writes anómalo with an acute accent; Portuguese anômalo can prompt the wrong accent, while unaccented *anomalo is incorrect.
example_tl: El patrón anómalo de consultas reveló una campaña coordinada, aunque cada cuenta individual parecía respetar los límites formales de la plataforma.
example_en: The anomalous query pattern revealed a coordinated campaign, although each individual account appeared to respect the platform's formal limits.
cloze: El patrón {{c1::anómalo}} de consultas reveló una campaña coordinada, aunque cada cuenta individual parecía respetar los límites formales de la plataforma.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Atípico is retained as a slightly less marked alternative in the same analytical context.

register: Neutral-formal and often emphatic in policy, journalism and historical analysis for something with no known prior equivalent.
trap: The fixed Spanish expression normally uses plural precedentes and no article: sin precedentes; it does not change with the noun's gender or number.
example_tl: La concentración sin precedentes de capacidad informática confiere a pocas empresas una influencia política que las autoridades nacionales apenas pueden contrarrestar.
example_en: The unprecedented concentration of computing capacity gives a few companies political influence that national authorities can barely counteract.
cloze: La concentración {{c1::sin precedentes}} de capacidad informática confiere a pocas empresas una influencia política que las autoridades nacionales apenas pueden contrarrestar.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. The expression is retained because its fixed plural form is a useful nonliteral production target. Self-review changed concede to the more idiomatic confiere una influencia.

register: Formal historical and analytical adjective for a person, document or event existing at the same time as another.
trap: English contemporaneous means co-occurring in time, not necessarily present-day; coetáneo and this sense of contemporáneo normally take a de complement.
example_tl: El informe fue coetáneo de las protestas, pero sus autores ignoraron documentos internos que ya contradecían la versión oficial.
example_en: The report was contemporaneous with the protests, but its authors ignored internal documents that already contradicted the official account.
cloze: El informe fue {{c1::coetáneo de}} las protestas, pero sus autores ignoraron documentos internos que ya contradecían la versión oficial.
note: Materially refines the underdetermined old_back contemporáneo by adding its de complement and blocking the competing present-day sense.

register: Neutral-critical in political and media analysis for conduct, coverage or institutions aligned with a party or faction rather than impartial.
trap: Partidario usually means a supporter and takes de; partisan bias or coverage is partidista, so old_back partidario selects the wrong construction here.
example_tl: La cobertura partidista convirtió una investigación judicial en arma electoral y omitió pruebas que incomodaban tanto al Gobierno como a la oposición.
example_en: Partisan coverage turned a judicial investigation into an electoral weapon and omitted evidence that troubled both the Government and the opposition.
cloze: La cobertura {{c1::partidista}} convirtió una investigación judicial en arma electoral y omitió pruebas que incomodaban tanto al Gobierno como a la oposición.
note: Materially corrects old_back partidario, which denotes a supporter or being in favour of something rather than partisan institutional bias.

register: Strongly critical in labour, economic and platform-policy writing for practices that unfairly profit from weaker actors or their work.
trap: The usual adjective in this abusive sense is explotador, not the literal-looking *explotativo; explotable instead means capable of being exploited.
example_tl: Las condiciones explotadoras obligan a los repartidores a asumir riesgos laborales mientras la plataforma conserva el control sobre tarifas, rutas y sanciones.
example_en: Exploitative conditions force couriers to assume occupational risks while the platform retains control over rates, routes and penalties.
cloze: Las condiciones {{c1::explotadoras}} obligan a los repartidores a asumir riesgos laborales mientras la plataforma conserva el control sobre tarifas, rutas y sanciones.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. The example supplies feminine plural agreement while the production headword remains the masculine lemma.

register: Formal scientific metaphor in political and economic analysis for a close relationship in which the parties sustain or benefit one another.
trap: Simbiótico implies reciprocal dependence or benefit, not mere coexistence; the parties can nevertheless possess very unequal power.
example_tl: La relación simbiótica entre plataformas y partidos amplifica mensajes polarizadores: las primeras obtienen atención y los segundos acceden a audiencias segmentadas.
example_en: The symbiotic relationship between platforms and parties amplifies polarising messages: the former gain attention and the latter access segmented audiences.
cloze: La relación {{c1::simbiótica}} entre plataformas y partidos amplifica mensajes polarizadores: las primeras obtienen atención y los segundos acceden a audiencias segmentadas.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. The example fixes the reciprocal political-economy metaphor and supplies feminine agreement. Self-review replaced potentially ambiguous pronouns with explicit former/latter forms.

register: Neutral-formal adjective for elements that differ markedly in type, origin, scale or character rather than forming a uniform set.
trap: Unlike Portuguese díspar, Spanish dispar and its plural dispares carry no written accent; the plural changes the ending but not the lexeme.
example_tl: El comité reunió fuentes dispares, desde archivos sindicales hasta registros empresariales, y descubrió que todas describían la misma precarización laboral.
example_en: The committee brought together disparate sources, from union archives to company records, and found that all described the same precarisation of labour.
cloze: El comité reunió fuentes {{c1::dispares}}, desde archivos sindicales hasta registros empresariales, y descubrió que todas describían la misma precarización laboral.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Retention is justified by the marked adjective, its irregular-looking plural and a genuine Portuguese interference risk.

register: Formal and uncommon in this evaluative sense; it describes a person, tone or attitude that judges others harshly or habitually finds fault.
trap: English censorious concerns severe disapproval, not institutional content removal; Spanish censor here has its older judgmental sense, with feminine censora.
example_tl: La actitud censora del columnista convirtió una discrepancia técnica en falta moral y dejó poco espacio para examinar los argumentos contrarios.
example_en: The columnist's censorious attitude turned a technical disagreement into a moral failing and left little room to examine the opposing arguments.
cloze: La actitud {{c1::censora}} del columnista convirtió una discrepancia técnica en falta moral y dejó poco espacio para examinar los argumentos contrarios.
note: Old_back gives a possible lemma but leaves the rare evaluative sense unspecified. Self-review retained censor only after anchoring harsh judgment and supplying feminine morphology.
